issue_context.title: Docker-proxy process uses 100% cpu and causes timeouts after 30k connections
issue_context.body:
### Description

When opening and closing 30k connections to redis sequentially using "docker-proxy" and "port mapping",
- docker-proxy process takes 100% cpu
- connection time increases significantly
- network timeouts (max. 3s) are reached

Running the same test with "network host" does not cause any errors.

### Reproduce

example repository: https://github.com/thbley/docker-proxy

example github pipeline which succeeds using "network host":
https://github.com/thbley/docker-proxy/actions/runs/8204298979/job/22438697761

example github pipeline which fails reproducable using "docker proxy" and "port mapping" after 30k connections:
https://github.com/thbley/docker-proxy/actions/runs/8204298979/job/22438697761

### Expected behavior

constant connection times using "docker-proxy" and "port mapping", no timeouts

comments:
As mentioned in https://github.com/docker/docs/issues/17312 , I disabled docker-proxy (= userland-proxy) locally on Ubuntu 22.04 (linux-image-6.2.0-36-generic) using:

```
cat /etc/docker/daemon.json 
{
        "userland-proxy": false
}

sudo /etc/init.d/docker stop
sudo /etc/init.d/docker start
```

With this change, the docker-proxy process is no longer started and the test finishes successfully with very good performance:
(with docker-proxy enabled, the test fails)

```
docker run --rm -it --name redis -d -p 6379:6379 redis:7.2-alpine
sleep 5
time docker run --rm -it --network host -v$(pwd):/var/www redistest php test.php
0.4921ms
922.2383ms
895.3366ms
1017.895ms
936.6858ms
948.3333ms
870.9774ms
893.5945ms
918.2863ms
891.0484ms

real    0m9,789s
user    0m0,016s
sys     0m0,017s
```

Regarding github actions, I used:

```
    - name: Disable userland proxy in docker daemon
      run: |
        sudo jq '.+{"userland-proxy":false}' /etc/docker/daemon.json > /tmp/daemon.json
        sudo mv /tmp/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json
        sudo systemctl restart docker.service
```

review_comments: This is not safe to do in a general-purpose TCP proxy. https://vincent.bernat.ch/en/blog/2014-tcp-time-wait-state-linux#socket-lingering
